title: Politeness and failure-path lab
description: Change the host condition to see how the scheduler preserves a remote site's budget while unrelated hosts remain available to the fleet.

nodes.label: URL frontier
nodes.detail: Selects the best candidate from hosts that are allowed to run. It cannot override a host's budget.

nodes.label: Robots cache
nodes.detail: Evaluates the path against cached robots rules and records the policy version used for the decision.

nodes.label: Host scheduler
nodes.detail: Maintains the next-allowed time, in-flight cap, backoff, and circuit state for one host.

nodes.label: Fetch worker
nodes.detail: Executes a single request under the scheduler's lease and classifies the outcome without choosing its own retry rate.

nodes.label: Remote host
nodes.detail: The website being crawled. Its responsiveness and policy are part of the crawler's operating contract.

nodes.label: Retry delay
nodes.detail: Holds only retryable work until a jittered backoff expires; it does not occupy a worker while waiting.

nodes.label: Review queue
nodes.detail: Retains bounded evidence for repeated failures, parser faults, or operator review instead of retrying forever.

nodes.label: Host telemetry
nodes.detail: Records policy decisions, delays, outcomes, bytes, and retries so operators can prove compliance and investigate complaints.

scenarios.label: Healthy host
scenarios.summary: The path is allowed, the host is past its next-allowed time, and a single leased fetch completes within the configured limits.
scenarios.result: One request is issued and the scheduler advances the next-allowed time before the next candidate can run.

scenarios.label: Crawl-delay wait
scenarios.summary: A valuable URL is allowed by robots policy but the host's next-allowed time has not arrived. The worker remains free for another eligible host.
scenarios.result: The URL waits in the host queue. Global capacity is filled from other hosts rather than violating this host's budget.

scenarios.label: Robots denial
scenarios.summary: The robots policy disallows the URL path. The scheduler records the decision but does not create a lease or a retry.
scenarios.result: No request leaves the crawler. A policy denial is a terminal scheduling outcome, not a transient failure.

scenarios.label: Timeout and backoff
scenarios.summary: A leased request times out. The scheduler lengthens the host delay, routes only the retryable item through backoff, and keeps other hosts independent.
scenarios.result: The retry waits with jitter. After bounded attempts, it moves to review instead of creating an unbounded retry storm.
